synonyms: Bothriochloa ischaemum var. songarica (Rupr. ex Fisch. & C.A.Mey.) Celarier & J.R.Harlan
Andropogon ischaemum var. songaricus Rupr. ex Fisch. & C.A.Mey.
taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Bothriochloa ischaemum at species rank and treats var. songarica, the Texas King Ranch bluestem name, as a synonym. Kew lists Texas as introduced, not native.
look_here_first: Start with the seedhead and nodes. King Ranch bluestem has smooth/glabrous nodes and a loose terminal head of only about 3–8 long fingerlike branches. The stems often kink/change angle at nodes and branch freely from a broad crown. That is very different from silver bluestem's dense cottony mass and cane bluestem's hairy nodes.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew/POWO lists the native range in temperate Eurasia and northwestern Africa and explicitly lists Texas among introduced regions. Texas A&M AgriLife describes King Ranch bluestem as an introduced, aggressive warm-season perennial. Texas Invasives evaluates the songarica concept and documents strong impacts on native plant community richness, including near-monocultures.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Wild roadside or prairie occurrence in Texas does not count as native-range evidence.

best_field_traits: perennial warm-season introduced bunchgrass, commonly to about 120 cm
broad flattened crown; can become stoloniferous under close grazing/mowing
light-green stems often change angle at nodes and branch freely
nodes glabrous in the familiar songarica/King Ranch form
leaves generally to about 20 cm long and 5 mm wide
upper culm relatively naked beneath inflorescence
inflorescence composed of about 3–8 long spicate fingerlike branches
both fertile and sterile spikelets may have slender bent/twisted awns
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Bothriochloa torreyana: Silver bluestem forms a dense silver-white cottony contracted panicle with many short rames; KR bluestem has only a few long fingerlike branches. Bothriochloa barbinodis: Cane bluestem has dense hairy rings at stem nodes and a fanlike inflorescence; KR bluestem's nodes are glabrous and head is more digitate/fingerlike.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Silver bluestem forms a dense silver-white cottony contracted panicle with many short rames; KR bluestem has only a few long fingerlike branches. Cane bluestem has dense hairy rings at stem nodes and a fanlike inflorescence; KR bluestem's nodes are glabrous and head is more digitate/fingerlike.
